newsitem.title: USA: New York Gov seeks federal aid for TWA Flight 800.
newsitem.headline: New York Gov seeks federal aid for TWA Flight 800.

text.p: New York Gov George Pataki on Friday said he had asked President Bill Clinton for federal aid to help repay the state and local governments for their assistance in responding to the TWA Flight 800 crash in July.

Pataki said that over $12 million had been spent so far in direct support of federal agencies that dealt with the crash off the Long Island shore, with Suffolk County, where the investigation was centered, running up a $5.8 million bill.
State agencies have spent more than $5 million, while New York City's total was $1.1 million. Nassau County spent $318,000.

"New Yorkers responded without concern for costs because people were in need--and we will do so again in the future if necessary. However, I believe federal assistance is both neceessary and appropriate in this case because of the magnitude of the disaster response effort," said Pataki, in prepared remarks.
